module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1041

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1041](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1041)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Polynomial MeasureTheory ENNReal

namespace Erdos1041

variable (n : ℕ) (f : ℂ[X]) (hn : n ≥ 2) (hnum : f.natDegree = n)
variable (h_monic : f.Monic)
variable (h : f.rootSet ℂ ⊆ Metric.ball 0 1)
include hn hnum h h_monic

/--
The length of a subset $s$ of $\mathbb{C}$ is defined to be its 1-dimensional
Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1(s)$.
-/
noncomputable def length (s : Set ℂ) : ℝ≥0∞ := μH[1] s

open scoped Classical in
/--
**Erdős–Herzog–Piranian Component Lemma** (Metric Properties of Polynomials, 1958):
If $f$ is a monic degree $n$ polynomial with all roots in the unit disk,
then some connected component
of $\{z \mid |f(z)| < 1\}$ contains at least two roots with multiplicity.

See p. 139, above Problem 5:
[EHP58] Erdős, P. and Herzog, F. and Piranian, G., _Metric properties of polynomials_.
  J. Analyse Math. (1958), 125-148.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 32]
theorem exists_connected_component_contains_two_roots :
    ∃ C, C ⊆ {z | ‖f.eval z‖ < 1} ∧ IsConnected C ∧
      2 ≤ (f.roots.filter (· ∈ C)).card := by
  sorry

/--
Let
$$ f(z) = \prod_{i=1}^{n} (z - z_i) \in \mathbb{C}[x] $$
with $|z_i| < 1$ for all $i$.

Conjecture: Must there always exist a path of length less than 2 in
$$ \{ z \in \mathbb{C} \mid |f(z)| < 1 \} $$
which connects two of the roots of $f$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 32]
theorem erdos_1041 :
    ∃ (z₁ z₂ : ℂ) (h : ({z₁, z₂} : Multiset ℂ) ≤ f.roots) (γ : Path z₁ z₂),
      Set.range γ ⊆ { z : ℂ | ‖f.eval z‖ < 1 } ∧ length (Set.range γ) < 2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos1041

reformulations.difference: The source says that a connected component contains at least two roots. Lean instead asks for a connected subset C of the sublevel set containing at least two roots, counted with multiplicity, without requiring C to be maximal.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Any such C is nonempty. Choose x ∈ C and enlarge C to connectedComponentIn S x, where S = {z | ‖f.eval z‖ < 1}. Connectedness puts C inside that component, and enlarging the set cannot decrease the cardinality of the filtered root multiset. Conversely, a component containing two roots is itself a suitable connected subset. The general equivalence, for arbitrary S and a multiset of points, was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: Lean bounds the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the path’s image, rather than the ordinary parametrized length of the particular path γ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This does not change the existential statement. A curve of ordinary length less than 2 has image of Hausdorff 1-measure at most that length. Conversely, the image K of a continuous path between distinct endpoints contains a simple arc A between those endpoints. If H¹(K) < 2, then H¹(A) ≤ H¹(K) < 2; an injectively parametrized arc of finite H¹ is rectifiable and its length equals H¹(A). This arc stays inside the original sublevel set. If the endpoints coincide, the multiset hypothesis requires two occurrences of that root, and the constant path has length zero in both formulations. Mathlib’s H¹ normalization was also checked on line segments.

review.notes: All three declarations were checked against the primary paper and the relevant definitions. The scratch file compiles successfully and verifies the component equivalence, the root-bound interpretation, complex factorization with multiplicities, Hausdorff measure on empty sets/singletons/segments, exclusion of degrees 0 and 1, and the admissible degree-2 example f = X². The root-pair condition genuinely requires two multiset occurrences. Direct access to erdosproblems.com/1041 returned a Cloudflare challenge despite a descriptive User-Agent; the mathematical statements were verified from EHP58 instead. The separately consulted Erdős-problem database records 1041 as “falsifiable,” meaning still open, so no status mismatch was found.
